title: Generate task-scoped context receipts without sacrificing reuse

state.decision_rationale: Deferred as a separate evidence artifact. Reopen only with a threat model for what an agent-run receipt can truthfully prove, plus privacy and redaction rules for tasks and outputs.

provenance.source_label: Claude Fable feature idea: task-scoped packets
provenance.review_target: Reported 39479-line MKTCTX/3 packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: @task plus edge-ranked selection plus a coverage statement becomes a reproducible, auditable artifact recording exactly what the agent was shown when it made a change.
feedback.normalized_claim: Support an optional task-bound receipt that identifies the reusable source-context packet, instruction, selection policy, and coverage used for an agent run.

current_behavior: @task is optional, appears once at the end, is framed as trust=instruction, and does not change manifest identity.
Keeping task outside manifest identity was a deliberate reuse property: the same source-context identity can accompany different tasks.
There is no separate run-receipt identity binding task digest, packet identity, model or agent, outputs, and selection execution.
evidence: src/context.test.ts: optional task appears once and does not change manifest identity

proposal.summary: Preserve reusable task-independent packet identity and evaluate a separate task or run receipt that cryptographically binds an instruction to the exact packet and selection evidence an agent consumed.
candidate_changes: Define distinct source-context identity and task or run-receipt identity.
Bind task digest, packet ID, selection policy or seed, coverage, generator, and optional agent-run metadata in the receipt.
Keep @task optional for direct prompting while allowing detached reusable tasks and receipts.
Specify privacy and redaction behavior for sensitive instructions or outputs.
non_goals: Do not make every reusable source packet task-specific by default.
Do not claim a packet alone proves what a hosted model actually received or retained.
Do not include private prompts or outputs in durable artifacts without explicit policy.

questions: What evidence is required to claim an agent was shown a packet rather than merely that a packet existed?
Should task text be embedded, content-addressed externally, encrypted, or redacted?
Does the receipt bind model, tool versions, outputs, and mutations or only input context?
risks: Receipts can overstate causal evidence when the model provider or host is not witnessed.
Task text can contain sensitive information and reduce packet reusability.
Binding rapidly changing run metadata can create many nearly identical artifacts.
evidence_needed: Threat and evidence model for local and hosted agent runs.
Prototype source-packet plus detached task-receipt workflow.
